# Java Edition protocol/Registries

> Minecraft Java snapshot: `1.20.6`  
> Protocol version: `766`  
> Source: [Java Edition protocol/Registries](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Registries?oldid=2765392)  
> Revision: `2765392` (`2024-02-26T18:46:32Z`)

> License: [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)

Registries are repositories of data that contain entries pertaining to certain aspects of the game, such as the world, the player, among others.

The ability for the server to send customized registries to the client was introduced in 1.16.3, which allows for a great deal of customization over certain features of the game.

# Format

The server sends these registries to the client via [Registry Data](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Registry_Data "Protocol") packet during the configuration phase.

| Packet ID | State | Bound To | Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x05 | Configuration | Client | Registry Data | [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | Information included below. |

The **Registry Data** field represents a list of all available registries in the form of a [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT"). Elements in this compound are defined by the [registry information](https://minecraft.wiki#Registry), associated with the registry's name, as shown in the example below:

```
{
    "minecraft:worldgen/biome": {
        "type": "minecraft:worldgen/biome",
        "value": [
            {
                "name": "minecraft:ocean",
                "id": 0,
                "element": { /* Element */ }
            },
            {
                "name": "minecraft:plains",
                "id": 1,
                "element": { /* Element */ }
            },
            { /* Registry Entry */ }
            ...
        ]
    },
    "minecraft:dimension_type": { /* Registry */ },
    "minecraft:chat_type": { /* Registry */ },
    ...
}
```

## Registry

The Registry [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") specifies the type of the registry, and a list of [registry entries](https://minecraft.wiki#Registry_Entry).

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Ambox_warning_pn.png/32px-Ambox_warning_pn.png?b6e1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Ambox_warning_pn.png "File:Ambox warning pn.png")

The name of the registry in the Registry Data is always the same to the registry type in the Notchian implementation.

| Name | Type | Notes | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| type | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | The type of the registry. |
| value | [List Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:list_tag "NBT") of [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | List of [registry entries](https://minecraft.wiki#Registry_Entry). |

## Registry Entry

The Registry Entry [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") specifies a single entry of a [Registry](https://minecraft.wiki#Registry).

| Name | Type | Notes | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | The name of the entry. |
| id | [Int Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:int_tag "NBT") | The protocol ID of the entry. |
| element | [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | The actual data of the entry. This field is context-dependent and is based on the **type** field of its [Registry](https://minecraft.wiki#Registry). |

# Available Registries

The current release specification allows for six different registries to be sent to the client, six of which are required. A brief explanation of each of them is presented below, along with the format of their entries' element field.

**Fields marked in \_\_ blue represent data for server-side exclusive operations, and thus have no visible impact on the client.**

## Armor Trim Material

The `minecraft:trim_material` registry. It defines various visual properties of trim materials in armors.

| Name | | | Type | | Meaning | | Values | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| asset\_name | | | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | | The trim color model to be rendered on top of the armor. The Notchian client uses the corresponding asset located at `trims/color_palettes`. | | Example: "minecraft:amethyst". | |
| ingredient | | | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | | The ingredient used. This has the visual effect of showing the trimmed armor model on the Smithing Table when the correct item is placed. | | Example: "minecraft:copper\_ingot". | |
| item\_model\_index | | | [Float Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:float_tag "NBT") | | Color index of the trim on the armor item when in the inventory. | | Default values vary between 0.1 and 1.0. | |
| override\_armor\_materials | | | Optional [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | | Asset for different types of armor materials, which overrides the value specified in the asset\_name field. The Notchian client uses this to give a darker color shade when a trim material is applied to armor of the same material, such as iron applied to iron armor. | | The key can be either:  - `leather` - `chainmail` - `iron` - `gold` - `diamond` - `turtle` - `netherite`   The value accepts the same values as asset\_name. | |
| description | | | [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") or [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | | The name of the trim material to be displayed on the armor tool-tip. Any styling used in this component is also applied to the trim pattern description. | | See [Text formatting](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Text_formatting "Text formatting"). | |

## Biome

The `minecraft:worldgen/biome` registry. It defines several aesthetic characteristics of the biomes present in the game.

Biome entries are referenced in the [Chunk Biomes](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Chunk_Biomes "Protocol") and [Chunk Data and Update Light](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Chunk_Data_and_Update_Light "Protocol") packets.

[Template:Warning2](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Template:Warning2?action=edit&redlink=1 "Template:Warning2 (page does not exist)")

| Name | | | Type | | Meaning | | Values | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| has\_precipitation | | | [Byte Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:byte_tag "NBT") | | Determines whether or not the biome has precipitation. | | 1: true, 0: false. | |
| temperature | | | [Float Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:float_tag "NBT") | | The temperature factor of the biome. Affects foliage and grass color if they are not explicitly set. | | The default values vary between -0.5 and 2.0. | |
| temperature\_modifier | | | Optional [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | | Modifier that affects the resulting temperature. | | Can be either:  - `none`, for a static temperature throughout the biome (aside from variations depending on the height). - `frozen`, for pockets of warm temperature (0.2) to be randomly distributed throughout the biome. This is used on frozen ocean variants in the Notchian client to simulate spots of unfrozen water, where it always rains instead of snowing. | |
| downfall | | | [Float Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:float_tag "NBT") | | The downfall factor of the biome. Affects foliage and grass color if they are not explicitly set. | | The default values vary between 0.0 and 1.0. | |
| effects | | | [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | | Biome special effects. | | See [Effects](https://minecraft.wiki#Effects). | |

| mood\_sound | | | Optional [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | | Additional ambient sound that plays in moody situations. Moodiness increases when blocks around the player are at both sky and block light level zero, and decreases otherwise. ## Chat Type

The `minecraft:chat_type` registry. It defines the different types of in-game chat and how they're formatted.

Chat type entries are referenced in the [Disguised Chat Message](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Disguised_Chat_Message "Protocol") and [Player Chat Message](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Player_Chat_Message "Protocol") packets.

| Name | | | Type | | Meaning | | Values | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| chat | | | [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | | The chat decoration. | | See [Decoration](https://minecraft.wiki#Decoration). | |
| narration | | | [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | | The narration decoration. | | See [Decoration](https://minecraft.wiki#Decoration). | |

### Decoration

| translation\_key | | | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | | The translation key representing the chat format. It can also be a formatting string directly. | | Example: "chat.type.text", which translates to "<%s> %s". | |
| style | | | Optional [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | | Optional styling to be applied on the final message. Not present in the narration decoration. | | See [Text formatting#Styling fields](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Text_formatting#Styling_fields "Text formatting"). | |

## Damage Type

The `minecraft:damage_type` registry. It defines the different types of damage an entity can sustain.

Damage type entries are referenced in the [Damage Event](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Damage_Event "Protocol") packet.

[Template:Warning2](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Template:Warning2?action=edit&redlink=1 "Template:Warning2 (page does not exist)")

| Name | Type | Meaning | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| message\_id | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | Id of the death message. The full message is displayed as `death.attack.<message_id>`. | Example: "onFire". |
| scaling | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | Whether the damage taken scales with the difficulty. | Can be either:  - `never` - `when_caused_by_living_non_player` - `always` |
| exhaustion | [Float Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:float_tag "NBT") | The amount of exhaustion caused when suffering this type of damage. | Default values are either 0.0 or 0.1. |
| effects | Optional [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | Effect played when the player suffers this damage, including the sound that is played. | Can be either:  - `hurt` - `thorns` - `drowning` - `burning` - `poking` - `freezing` |
| death\_message\_type | Optional [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | Defines how the death message is constructed. | Can be either:  - `default`, for the message to be built normally. - `fall_variants`, for the most significant fall damage to be considered. - `intentional_game_design`, for [MCPE-28723](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE-28723) to be considered as an argument when translating the message. |

## Dimension Type

The `minecraft:dimension_type` registry. It defines the types of dimension that can be attributed to a world, along with all their characteristics.

Dimension type entries are referenced in the [Login (play)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Login_(play) "Protocol") and [Respawn](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Respawn "Protocol") packets.

| Name | Type | Meaning | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fixed\_time | Optional [Long Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:long_tag "NBT") | If set, the time of the day fixed to the specified value. | Allowed values vary between 0 and 24000. |
| has\_skylight | [Byte Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:byte_tag "NBT") | Whether the dimension has skylight access or not. | 1: true, 0: false. |
| has\_ceiling | [Byte Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:byte_tag "NBT") | Whether the dimension has a bedrock ceiling or not. When true, causes lava to spread faster. | 1: true, 0: false. |
| ultrawarm | [Byte Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:byte_tag "NBT") | Whether the dimensions behaves like the nether (water evaporates and sponges dry) or not. Also causes lava to spread thinner. | 1: true, 0: false. |
| natural | [Byte Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:byte_tag "NBT") | When false, compasses spin randomly. When true, nether portals can spawn zombified piglins. | 1: true, 0: false. |
| coordinate\_scale | [Double Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:double_tag "NBT") | The multiplier applied to coordinates when traveling to the dimension. | Allowed values vary between 1e-5 (0.00001) and 3e7 (30000000). |
| bed\_works | [Byte Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:byte_tag "NBT") | Whether players can use a bed to sleep. | 1: true, 0: false. |

| min\_y | [Int Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:int_tag "NBT") | The minimum Y level. | Allowed values vary between -2032 and 2031, and must also be a multiple of 16. min\_y + height cannot exceed 2032. |
| height | [Int Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:int_tag "NBT") | The maximum height. | Allowed values vary between 16 and 4064, and must also be a multiple of 16. min\_y + height cannot exceed 2032. |

| infiniburn | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | A resource location defining what block tag to use for infiniburn. | "#" or minecraft resource "#minecraft:...". |
| effects | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | Defines special dimensional effects, which includes:  - Cloud level: Height at which clouds appear, if at all. - Sky type: Whether it's the normal sky with sun and moon; the low-visibility, foggy sky of the nether; or the static sky of the end. - Forced light map: Whether a bright light map is forced, siimilar to the night vision effect. - Constant ambient light: Whether blocks have shade on their faces. | Can be either:  - `minecraft:overworld`, for clouds at 192, normal sky type, normal light map and normal ambient light. - `minecraft:the_nether`, for **no clouds**, nether sky type, normal light map and **constant** ambient light. - `minecraft:the_end`, for **no clouds**, end sky type, **forced** light map and normal ambient light. |
| ambient\_light | [Float Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:float_tag "NBT") | How much light the dimension has. Used as interpolation factor when calculating the brightness generated from sky light. | The default values are 0.0 and 0.1, 0.1 for the nether and 0.0 for the other dimensions. |
| piglin\_safe | [Byte Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:byte_tag "NBT") | Whether piglins shake and transform to zombified piglins. | 1: true, 0: false. |
| has\_raids | [Byte Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:byte_tag "NBT") | Whether players with the Bad Omen effect can cause a raid. | 1: true, 0: false. |
| monster\_spawn\_light\_level | [Int Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:int_tag "NBT") or [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | During a monster spawn attempt, this is the maximum allowed light level for it to succeed. It can be either a fixed value, or one of several types of distributions. | Can be either:  - as a [Int Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:int_tag "NBT"): Allowed values vary between 0 and 15. - as a [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT"): See [Integer distribution](https://minecraft.wiki#Integer_distribution). |
| monster\_spawn\_block\_light\_limit | [Int Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:int_tag "NBT") | Maximum allowed block light level monster spawn attempts to happen. | Allowed values vary between 0 and 15. The default values are 0 and 15, 15 for the nether (where monsters can spawn anywhere) and 0 for other dimensions (where monsters can only spawn naturally in complete darkness). |

### Integer distribution

Integer providers can be either declared as constants with a [Int Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:int_tag "NBT"), or in a structured [Compound Tags](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") for specific distribution types. For the latter, the following format is used.

[Template:Need Info](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Template:Need_Info?action=edit&redlink=1 "Template:Need Info (page does not exist)")

| Name | Type | Meaning | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| type | [String Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:string_tag "NBT") | The type of distribution. | Can be either:  - `minecraft:constant`, for constant values, similarly to when declared as a [Int Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:int_tag "NBT"). - `minectaft:uniform`, for uniformly distributed values between the specified range. - `minecraft:biased_to_bottom`, for values biased towards the lower end, between the specified range. - `minecraft:clamped`, for uniformly distributed values, clamped inside a range. - `minecraft:weighted_list`, for a weighted list of multiple distributions. - `minecraft:clamped_normal`, for normally distributed values, clamped inside a range. |
| value | [Compound Tag](https://minecraft.wiki/w/NBT#Specification:compound_tag "NBT") | Extra data pertaining to the type of distribution. | Depends on the type of distribution. |
